title: Lattice layout and quantum resonance implications
html:
Remark. Lattice layout and quantum resonance implications

Connecting the resonance condition (crystal probe of q) to concrete lattice experiments requires three undeveloped structural ingredients:

  1. Lattice--leaf commensurability. For a d-dimensional Bravais lattice with basis vectors \{\vec{a}_i\}, the resonance condition (crystal probe of q) requires Diophantine matching between the reciprocal lattice vectors \{\vec{G}_j\} and the characteristic wave-vectors of the q-torsion leaves. The lattice symmetry group acts on the space of q-harmonic forms. This selects a finite set of resonance channels indexed by the irreducible representations of the point group.
  2. Frustration and non-monotonicity. When the lattice hosts internal rotational degrees of freedom (e.g., magnetic rotor arrays), the coupling to q-torsion may become non-monotonic in a control parameter like interlayer separation or applied field. The q-deformed Reeb flow (q-Reeb flow) introduces a preferred orientation that competes with the lattice symmetry. This competition produces frustrated configurations where energy dissipation maximizes at an intermediate commensurability.
  3. Quantum coherence at the lattice scale. Kagome many-body interference indicates that quantum coherence extends over macroscopic lattice domains. In our framework, the correlation length of the q-harmonic forms on the brane bounds this coherence length. This correlation length depends on the local curvature of the CR manifold M. Establishing this bound quantitatively requires computing the q-deformed propagator on the lattice. We leave this to future work.
